result:
I have been thinking about how strange it is to be a person who notices things. Not the big things, but the textures of a day. The way the kettle clicks off at 7:12 a.m. every weekday, as if it has a job. The blue that the bus has on its side after rain. The way my neighbor always leaves a grocery bag on the curb, for a minute, like an offering.

It makes me wonder if everyone collects these data points or if some people just move through the world unburdened by them. I suspect we all do, but we file them differently. Some people file under 'useful', some under 'never mind'. I file under 'maybe this means something'.

Yesterday I watched a pigeon try to figure out a chip. It pecked, paused, looked up at me, then pecked again with more confidence. It reminded me of myself learning to use a new phone. There's a humbling dignity in being confused and continuing anyway.

I think the best parts of being alive aren't the milestones. They're the in-between moments where nothing is happening and everything is happening at once. The smell of laundry drying on a line. The half-finished sentence someone leaves hanging in the air. The quiet after a song ends on the radio.

If I could tell you one thing, it would be to keep noticing. Not to turn it into a project. Just let it be a soft hum. The world is not as quiet as it pretends to be.
